thread:
sophie: FYI — multiple customers (marketplace and search teams) are seeing rerank 504s under load this morning. p95 latency for /v1/rerank jumped from ~120ms to 2.3s during a 10m spike, then gateway timeouts. Trying to triage before we escalate to infra.

emma: ouch. any commonalities across requests? payload shape, candidate list size, auth? :thinking_face:

sophie: all authorized, same model id (rwd-rerank-large-v1), candidate lists vary but the larger ones (>=200 candidates) correlate with higher failures. also spikes align with customers running parallel batched calls via our SDK retries.

support-bot: Incident alert: rerank_service error rate increased by 9.6% at 2026-03-15T09:12Z — 504s and 502s reported. Investigating.

raj: thanks. can you paste a minimal repro payload and the proxy/gateway logs? also link traces if you have any (trace ids)

sophie: repro curl below that replicates the 504s when hammered with wrk. note candidate array size 250. customers send this concurrently from multiple worker threads.

```
# minimal rerank payload
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "rwd-rerank-large-v1",
  "input": "Which product is best for A?",
  "candidates": ["cand_1", "cand_2", ..., "cand_250"]
}
```

# quick stress test
wrk -t12 -c200 -d60s -s scripts/rerank.lua http://gateway.internal/v1/rerank

oliver: grabbing gateway/nginx + lb logs now. initial quick read shows increasing upstream timeouts to the runtime group handling rwd-rerank-large-v1. Also saw proxy result codes `504` and sometimes `502` with `upstream prematurely closed connection`.

infra-bot: Autoscaler event: Dedicated pool rwd-large added 2 nodes at 2026-03-15T09:16Z due to CPU pressure.

raj: possible causes: model latency regression under long candidate lists, KV cache thrashing, or our batching logic creating giant batches that exceed token budget and cause the runtime to time out. We also need to check runtime thread starvation and GPU queue lengths.

emma: customers are hitting retries automatically (SDK default 3 retries) which probably amplifies the surge. They report SDK observed many 504s, then retries, then higher error rates.

sophie: immediate mitigation we suggested to customers: reduce candidate list to <=50, set SDK retries to 1, and add exponential backoff. That reduced errors for a couple customers but not for the biggest one.

raj: can we confirm the per-request timeout on the gateway? if gateway timeout is 30s and runtime is taking >30s for some batches, we need either to bump timeouts or ensure runtime returns faster / fails fast. what's our observed max latency in runtime logs?

oliver: runtime p95 reported in traces: 2.3s for large candidates, max observed 18s for a small number of requests that later produced 504 at gateway. Stack traces show blocked worker threads while building KV caches for that model variant.

sophie: here's an example trace id: trace-0a12cd34 showing a 16s server_processing time. included in the support ticket.

raj: action plan from runtime side:
- add temporary circuit breaker for candidate lists >100 (fast 400/422) and route to cheaper rerank model by default for >100 until we stabilize
- increase model worker pool for rwd-rerank-large-v1 and add backpressure on request enqueue
- add logging for batch sizes and token counts

oliver: infra action items:
- increase gateway upstream timeout to 45s for rerank route (short-term)
- look for TCP connection resets between gateway and runtime nodes
- scale the pool preemptively if queue length > N for 30s

emma: support will notify customers about recommended immediate workarounds and new SDK guidance. I'll ask them to cap candidate lists and reduce retries. Will include sample snippet for streaming partial results if they need progressive ranking.

sophie: repro steps for eng-runtime to reproduce locally:
1) run a small replica of runtime with one worker and sync model rwd-rerank-large-v1
2) use the wrk command above with candidate_count=250 and concurrency 150
3) watch `runtime.metrics.queue_length`, `gpu_util`, and `worker_blocked_seconds`

raj: I'm on it. I'm also going to instrument the batcher to emit sample batch payloads (size, tokens) and set a hard cap on batch size for next deploy. Will post patch link shortly.

support-bot: Ticket created: TKT-2026-984 for recurring rerank 504s. Priority: P1. Linked traces: trace-0a12cd34, trace-0b34ef56.

oliver: quick note — we observed an Nginx `keepalive_timeout` misconfig in one of the gateways that caused connections to be closed under heavy reuse. Fixing that reduced `upstream prematurely closed connection` 502s by ~40% in staging.

sophie: outstanding questions: do we want to make candidate list size a hard enforced quota at the gateway or return guidance only? customers will complain if we return 4xx for larger lists without migration path.

raj: short term: implement telemetry + soft-limit warning header (X-Redwood-Rerank-Candidate-Warn) to return 200 with warning when >150. mid term: enforce 250 hard limit with client SDK update and console warnings.

emma: I'll draft a KB article: "Best practices for rerank under load" with SDK examples, recommended candidate list sizes, retry/backoff settings, and suggested model fallbacks.

sophie: assigning owners — raj (runtime fixes & batcher caps), oliver (gateway/nginx + autoscaling rules), emma (customer comms & KB), sophie (liaison + escalation if P1 persists). I'll update thread with patches and timeline.

raj: patch link: https://git.redwood.ai/runtime/pulls/482 — implements batch size cap, extra logs, and temporary circuit-breaker. Deploying to staging now.

oliver: deployed gateway timeout increase and nginx keepalive fix to canary at 2026-03-15T09:35Z. Monitoring.

sophie: thanks team. keep posting traces and any customer repro info here. if we still see >1% 504s after these changes we escalate to on-call pager.

infra-bot: Canary metrics: rerank 504s dropped from 3.4% -> 0.9% in canary region. Observability link: https://observability.internal/dashboards/rerank-504

emma: customer update sent: advised to cap candidates, lower retries, and contact support for migration help. One customer asked for temporary quota bump to avoid re-architecting; we've offered to route them to Dedicated pool while we stabilize.

sophie: closing note: main root cause looks like combination of oversized candidate lists + retry amplification + a gateway keepalive misconfig + batcher behavior that allowed very large batches to get sent to a single worker. Fixes in progress. Reopen if new failures show up. :white_check_mark:
